title: Checks for nested assignments.
summary: While this is in most cases already a type mismatch, the result of an assignment being () can throw off people coming from languages like python or C, where such assignments return a copy of the assigned value. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Check if a generic is defined both in the bound predicate and in the where clause.
summary: It can be confusing for developers when seeing bounds for a generic in multiple places. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks to see if multiple versions of a crate are being used.
summary: This bloats the size of targets, and can lead to confusing error messages when structs or traits are used interchangeably between different versions of a crate. Clippy puts this lint in the cargo group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for multiple inherent implementations of a struct
summary: Splitting the implementation of a type makes the code harder to navigate. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for unsafe blocks that contain more than one unsafe operation.
summary: Combined with undocumented_unsafe_blocks, this lint ensures that each unsafe operation must be independently justified. Combined with unused_unsafe, this lint also ensures elimination of unnecessary unsafe blocks through refactoring. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for public functions that have no #[must_use] attribute, but return something not already marked must-use, have no mutable arg and mutate no statics.
summary: Not bad at all, this lint just shows places where you could add the attribute. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for a #[must_use] attribute on unit-returning functions and methods.
summary: Unit values are useless. The attribute is likely a remnant of a refactoring that removed the return type. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: This lint checks for functions that take immutable references and return mutable ones.
summary: This will not trigger if no unsafe code exists as there are multiple safe functions which will do this transformation Creating a mutable reference which can be repeatably derived from an immutable reference is unsound as it allows creating multiple live mutable references to the same object. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for instances of mut mut references.
summary: This is usually just a typo or a misunderstanding of how references work. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for &mut Mutex::lock calls
summary: Mutex::lock is less efficient than calling Mutex::get_mut. In addition you also have a statically guarantee that the mutex isn’t locked, instead of just a runtime guarantee. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for loops with a range bound that is a mutable variable.
summary: One might think that modifying the mutable variable changes the loop bounds. It doesn’t. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for sets/maps with mutable key types.
summary: All of HashMap, HashSet, BTreeMap and BtreeSet rely on either the hash or the order of keys be unchanging, so having types with interior mutability is a bad idea. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of Mutex<X> where an atomic will do.
summary: Using a mutex just to make access to a plain bool or reference sequential is shooting flies with cannons. std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool and std::sync::atomic::AtomicPtr are leaner and faster. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of Mutex<X> where X is an integral type.
summary: Using a mutex just to make access to a plain integer sequential is shooting flies with cannons. std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize is leaner and faster. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.
